Indices of features

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/getFeatureIndices.R
getFeatureIndices.Rd

Calculates indices that describe how the abundance of each feature varies over the samples, for example over time within each subject: how much (variance, coefficient of variation), in what form (skewness, kurtosis, bimodality) and how persistently (stability). These are the feature-level counterparts of the sample-level indices of getAlpha().

getFeatureIndices(x, ...)

addFeatureIndices(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
getFeatureIndices(
  x,
  assay.type = "counts",
  index = c("variance", "cv", "skewness", "kurtosis", "bimodality"),
  group = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
addFeatureIndices(
  x,
  assay.type = "counts",
  index = c("variance", "cv", "skewness", "kurtosis", "bimodality"),
  name = index,
  group = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

SummarizedExperiment.

...

additional arguments passed to getBimodality() and getStability(), such as time.col.

assay.type

Character scalar. Specifies the name of the assay used in calculation. (Default: "counts")

index

Character vector. Specifies the indices to calculate. (Default: c("variance", "cv", "skewness", "kurtosis", "bimodality"))

group

NULL or Character scalar. Specifies a column from colData(x) that defines the groups, for example subjects, within which the indices are calculated. (Default: NULL)

name

Character vector. Specifies the column names for the indices, one per index. (Default: index)

Value

getFeatureIndices returns a DataFrame with one row per feature. addFeatureIndices adds the results to rowData(x).

Details

The available indices are:

  • "variance": sample variance.

  • "cv": coefficient of variation, the standard deviation divided by the mean.

  • "skewness": moment coefficient of skewness.

  • "kurtosis": moment coefficient of kurtosis (3 for a normal distribution).

  • "bimodality": see getBimodality().

  • "stability": see getStability(); requires time.col.

With group, each index is calculated within each group, for example within each subject, and the columns are named <index>_<group>.

See also

getAlpha()

Examples

library(miaTime)

# A defined community of 16 species in three replicate bioreactors
data(minimalgut)
tse <- transformAssay(minimalgut, method = "relabundance")

# Indices of each species over time, within each bioreactor
getFeatureIndices(tse, assay.type = "relabundance",
    index = c("cv", "stability"), group = "StudyIdentifier",
    time.col = "Time.hr")
